1.6StagesofaRiverCourse
The whole length of the river is termed as its course.The course of a river has three distinct
stages. This includes the upper course, the middle course, and the lower course. They have
different land features, that are formed by the erosional and depositional work of the river.
TheUppercourse
The upper course of a river is also called the youth stage. This is the mountainous stage of the
river. River forms several features in its upper course e.g. valleys, waterfalls, and gorges.
In this stage the speed of the river water is fast as it flows on steep slopes. The river carries
stones, boulders, and particles as its load.The river erodes its bed downwards with the help of
its load, carving out V-shapedvalleys. These valleys are narrow, deep and steep.
When the river flows from hard to soft rocks, the soft rocks are eroded away, leaving behind
overhanging hardrocks.The riverplunges down as a waterfall from the overhanging hard rocks.
Niagara Falls in North America is one of the most famous waterfalls. Basin shaped land features,
termedasplunge pools,areformed under waterfalls by the natural force of falling water.
ii) TheMiddlecourse
The middle course of a river is called its mature stage. In the mature stage river water loses its
speed andforce as it is flowing ina plain area. It can onlycarry light and small particles of rocks
and it begins to deposit its heavy loads. A River takes winding courses in this stage; many
tributaries join it, resulting an increase in its volume.
